provenance.summary: Generated from Nimiq's published signed-message format with a throwaway key. NOT captured from a phone. Every byte below is reproducible from the sources listed in `derivedFrom` plus `testKey.privateKey`.
derivedFrom: nimiq/keyguard src/lib/Key.js — Key.signMessage(): buffer = utf8(prefix) + utf8(message.byteLength.toString(10)) + message; hash = Nimiq.Hash.computeSha256(buffer); the Ed25519 signature is over that 32-byte hash, never over the message.
nimiq/hub client/HubApi.ts — public static readonly MSG_PREFIX = '\x16Nimiq Signed Message:\n' (23 bytes: 0x16 is the length of the 22-byte label that follows).
nimiq/hub sign-message API reference — states the signed bytes verbatim as sign( sha256( '\x16Nimiq Signed Message:\n' + message.length + message ) ).
notDerivedFrom: @nimiq/mini-app-sdk 0.1.0 — dist/provider.js sign() only forwards { method: 'sign', params: { message } } over the native bridge. It never touches the bytes, so it cannot tell you what gets signed.

@nimiq/core 2.7.1 — ships no message-signing or message-verifying helper, and the string 'Nimiq Signed Message' appears nowhere in its wasm. SignatureProof.verify(data) verifies transaction data, not prefixed messages.
provenance.proves: The server verifies exactly the bytes Nimiq's documented format produces, and refuses the same signature under the `raw` scheme.
provenance.doesNotProve: That the Nimiq Pay build on any given handset follows that documented format. The wallet side of the mini-app bridge is closed source; only a capture from a real device settles it.
provenance.howToReplaceWithACapture: Open a live drop inside Nimiq Pay, tap the claim button, approve, then read window.__nimiqRawLog (web/src/sdk/adapter.ts records every sign() request and response). Copy the request `message` and the response `publicKey`/`signature` into this file, set deviceCaptured to true, replace `derivedFrom` with the device/app version, and delete `testKey`. test/device-sign.test.ts must still pass unchanged — that is the whole point of it.

walletReportedAddress: NQ07 CDQK RDEC P1FY VN23 UL49 UFMM S8U2 X2RX

rawSchemeCounterExample.note: The SAME key over the SAME message under the `raw` scheme: Ed25519 straight over the UTF-8 message bytes, no prefix and no hash. Present so the test can prove the mismatch diagnostic fires in BOTH directions, not just the one that broke production.

testKey.note: Throwaway. Deterministic, non-secret, never funded, never used on any network — the same convention as CUSTODY_KEY_HEX in test/boot-binding.test.ts. It is here so the committed signatures can be re-derived and proven un-fudged; Ed25519 signing is deterministic (RFC 8032), so regenerating must reproduce them byte for byte. Delete this block when a real device capture replaces the vector.
